title: The Metamorphosis, Kafka
subject: litterature
description: Gregor Samsa wakes up transformed into an insect. Kafka shows how the family and society reject those who can no longer work.

hero.hook: One morning, Gregor Samsa wakes up transformed: the phrase that sums up an entire era.

blocks.text: Published in **1915**,  opens with one of the most famous incipits in literature: “One morning, coming out of a troubled dream, Gregor Samsa woke up transformed into a monstrous insect. » The original title in German is *The Verwandlung*. **Franz Kafka**, born in **1883** and died in **1924**, does not offer a fantastic tale, but the archetype of modern dehumanization. [[The Metamorphosis]]

Written in record time in November **1912**, the work explores what happens when an individual stops being productive. He instantly loses his human status in the eyes of his people. The absurd transformation reveals an alienation already at work before the physical change.

sections.title: The genesis of an absurd masterpiece

blocks.text: Kafka wrote the short story in **1912**, during a period of intense creativity in Prague. He treats the transformation with **clinical realism**: no supernatural explanation, no search for cause. The focus is entirely on the material and family consequences.

blocks.caption: Gregor's Metamorphosis: Kafka forbade the insect to be depicted on the cover.

blocks.text: Kafka strictly forbade his publisher from drawing the insect on the cover, preferring that the reader imagine their own version of the horror.

His friend  disobeyed Kafka's last wishes. Kafka demanded the destruction of his manuscripts. Brod published them posthumously, thus saving a work that became  par excellence. The adjective designates an absurd, oppressive and illogical situation. [[Max Brod]] [[Kafkaesque]]

Before his transformation, **Gregor Samsa** was **traveling salesman**, traveling sales representative. He is the sole financial support of his family. His life is a series of exhausting journeys and submission to a tyrannical leader. He secretly dreams of resigning, but the family debt prevents him from doing so.

By becoming a “vermin”, Gregor makes visible a dehumanization already at work. The German term *Ungeziefer* designates an impure, rejected, worthless animal. Paradoxically, this monstrous form finally frees him from the 5 a.m. train: he no longer has to go to work.

Initially, sister **Grete** feeds Gregor and cleans his room devotedly. But time erodes this solidarity. To survive, each member of the family works again: the father finds a job, the mother sews, Grete becomes a saleswoman. Gregor becomes a shameful burden.

The Samsas rent rooms to , tenants who take their meals in the house. Gregor is reduced to living in hiding. When Grete declares that they must "get rid of him", Gregor starves himself to death. He understands that he no longer has his place in this family that has become “normal” again. [[boarders]]

sections.title: The survival of the living and the end of the nightmare

blocks.text: Gregor's death is not a tragedy for the family, but a **delivery**. They go for a tram ride, already thinking about Grete's wedding. Gregor is completely erased from their memory in a few weeks. The rediscovered normality proves more terrifying than the metamorphosis itself.

blocks.caption: Prague at the beginning of the 20th century: the city where Kafka wrote his short story.

blocks.text: The short story illustrates how work and family structure crush the individual as soon as he or she ceases to be economically useful. Kafka describes a bureaucratic world where man is only a function. Family love depends on productivity. The absurdity is not in the metamorphosis itself, but in the reaction of those close to him, who prefer erasure of the patient to compassion.
uses the absurd transformation of a man into an insect to denounce alienation through work and the fragility of links based on economic utility. [[The Metamorphosis]]
